controls.reason: Rate, volume, size, concurrency, and resource limits are five explicit typed policy bounds with units and scope bindings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any missing, unlimited, malformed, or conflicting limit fails; explicit versioned bounds pass.

controls.reason: Where schemas are practical and which interfaces need them require architecture judgment, while a schema reference does not prove meaningful coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team can mark a complex but schema-capable interface impractical and omit it. All selected interfaces pass while machine-verifiable coverage is missing.

controls.reason: Materiality, interface inventories, and adequate consumer-driven compatibility behavior require judgment and complete test oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Registered interfaces can pass smoke contracts while an omitted material callback or error shape breaks a consumer. Tests pass but compatibility is not maintained.

controls.reason: Early enough for consumers to act has no objective lead-time threshold and depends on complete consumer inventories and migration circumstances.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered consumers can receive a timeline one day before retirement, which fields call early. Records pass while consumers cannot reasonably migrate.

controls.reason: Credential and production-data inventories cannot prove absence of unknown secrets or uncontrolled data copies in every integration path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known fixtures can use test tokens while an unlisted environment variable contains a production key or copied personal data. Tests pass but production material is used.

controls.reason: A capability and limitation list cannot prove that simulator behavior is described completely or accurately.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A stub can claim to reproduce retries while omitting ordering differences. Fields exist but consumers are misled about reproduced behavior.

controls.reason: Fixtures, schemas, protocol captures, simulators, and reference data are a fixed five-class artifact set with immutable version bindings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, mutable, or unversioned test assets fail; exact bound versions pass.

controls.reason: Approved maximum message, file, batch, record, and concurrency values and bound execution results make threshold testing exact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing maximum case, wrong test input, or absent result fails; execution at every policy maximum passes.

controls.reason: Five named failure fixtures do not prove correct root-cause distinction across combined, nested, timing, and ambiguous failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A network timeout caused by provider overload can be mislabeled consumer failure while simple fixtures pass. The suite cannot distinguish real failures reliably.

controls.reason: Immutable component-version and configuration identifiers tied to integration results make evidence provenance an exact referential-integrity fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, stale, ambiguous, or mismatched result bindings fail; exact linked evidence passes.

controls.reason: Configuration, identity, topology, provider, data, and runtime state inventories are not complete enough to prove all integration-production drift is detected.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Compared manifests can match while a production gateway policy differs outside the inventory. Tests pass but material drift remains.

controls.reason: Repeated resets cannot prove deterministic reconstruction across all shared state, timing, failures, hidden stores, and concurrency.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two fixtures can reconstruct identically while an omitted cache or race leaves stale data. Tests pass but shared state is not deterministically reset.

controls.reason: Representative failure selection is a contextual judgment and the failure inventory can omit material cases.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A trivial parsing failure can be retained while a production race is excluded as nonrepresentative. Regression evidence exists but escaped risk is not covered.

controls.reason: A transition inventory cannot prove completeness across hidden state, history, permissions, identities, keys, configuration, and metadata.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed tables can be present while a legacy permission store or encryption key is omitted. The inventory passes but transition scope is incomplete.

controls.reason: Data-class completeness and authoritative source or target selection require domain and governance judgment for every transition phase.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A data class can be omitted or the wrong replica named authoritative. Records pass but transition authority is unsafe.

controls.reason: Mapping rules, transformations, defaults, rejected-record behavior, and reconciliation criteria form a fixed versioned transition-contract schema.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, implicit, conflicting, or unbound definitions fail; runtime conformance is tested separately.

controls.reason: Identifier and relationship inventories can omit records, and documented replacements do not prove complete referential preservation across the dataset.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Sample links can preserve correctly while an unlisted foreign key is lost. Records pass but relationships are not preserved.

controls.reason: Consent, retention, legal-hold, authorship, and audit preservation require legal authority and complete data lineage, not record presence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A transition can copy timestamps while dropping a legal hold or invalid consent restriction. Fields pass but legal history is not preserved.

controls.reason: Units, precision, zones, calendars, encodings, normalization, and code sets have large domains and semantic equivalence not exhausted by fixtures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Common values can pass while a DST boundary or Unicode normalization changes meaning. Validation exists but transition data is still wrong.

controls.reason: The universal no-loss claim spans every field, type, boundary, transformation, and unsupported value beyond selected records.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known cases can pass while a large decimal rounds or an unknown field disappears. Tests pass but silent loss remains.

controls.reason: Invalid, duplicate, orphaned, stale, and conflicting records form a fixed five-class treatment-policy schema.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, implicit, or contradictory handling for any class fails; explicit versioned treatment passes.

controls.reason: Representative volume, skew, age, and edge-case distributions require empirical and domain judgment, and finite samples cannot prove transition behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A small uniform sample can be called representative while production has old skewed records. Tests pass but the actual transition may fail.

controls.reason: Duration, resource use, locking, service impact, and recovery time are five explicit execution metrics with units and test bindings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, malformed, or unbound measurements fail; the control asks to measure rather than meet a threshold.

controls.reason: Which transitions are long and whether checkpoints truly resume safely require runtime, data, and interruption oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration can expose checkpoints but duplicate rows after a later crash, or be mislabeled short. Fields pass but resumability is not proven.
